description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of experts and the normalized average gate value across different task domains for a sparse architectural large language model. The x-axis, labeled “Experts,” is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 64, with tick marks at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. The y-axis, labeled “Normalized Average Gate Value,” is on a linear scale ranging from 0.00 to 0.20, with tick marks at intervals of 0.05. Seven solid-colored lines represent different task domains: “Intent” (orange), “Summary” (blue), “Law” (yellow), “Translation” (purple), “Math” (gray), and “Code” (green), each accompanied by a shaded region indicating variance or confidence interval. A dashed black horizontal line near y = 0.015 serves as a baseline reference. All task-specific lines begin at higher gate values when the number of experts is low (e.g., “Translation” starts near 0.17 at 1 expert) and decline sharply as the number of experts increases, converging toward the baseline by 64 experts (e.g., “Translation” drops to approximately 0.005 at 64 experts). The shaded regions for each line also narrow as the number of experts grows, suggesting reduced variance in gate values at higher expert counts.
